newsitem.title: CHILE: AIG to invest in Mexico pension manager.
newsitem.headline: AIG to invest in Mexico pension manager.

text.p: American International Group Inc (AIG) said it will invest $100 million in a pension fund manager in Mexico which will start operating next month.
"Mexico is a very attractive market for AIG as it has enormous potential for (recruiting) savers," it said.
The fund, to be called Previnter, is the result of a deal between AIG, Bank of Boston Corp, Canada's Bank of Nova Scotia and Mexican bank Inverlat, said the statement issued in Santiago.
The fund will operate throughout Mexico and employ a salesforce of more than 3,000, it said.
AIG owns the Union pension fund in Chile, whose private pension system is the most developed in Latin America.
Mexico is the latest country to adopt the Chilean-designed scheme, which already been copied in Argentine, Peru and Colombia.
